claim: For the repulsive Lieb–Liniger Hamiltonian \(H_N=-\sum_{i=1}^{N}\partial_{x_i}^{2}+2g\sum_{i<j}\delta(x_i-x_j)\) on the bosonic half-line with attractive Robin boundary condition \(\partial_{x_i}\Psi|_{x_i=0}=-\kappa\Psi\), where \(g>0\), \(N\ge2\), and \(\kappa>(N-1)g\), the symmetric wavefunction \(\Psi_N=C_N\exp[-\sum_{j=1}^{N}(\kappa-(j-1)g)x_{(j)}]\) is an exact positive ground state with energy \(E_N=-\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(\kappa-jg)^2\). Its separation energy from the \((N-1)\)-particle boundary cluster is \(\Delta_N=(\kappa-(N-1)g)^2\), while the mean outermost interparticle gap is \(1/[2(\kappa-(N-1)g)]\); hence the final binding gap closes quadratically and the outer gap diverges inversely at the boundary-string threshold.
scientific_limitations: Continuum half-line with repulsive contact coupling and one attractive Robin boundary only.
The result constructs the explicit fully boundary-bound state and does not classify all excited states or all possible states below threshold.
Independent audit and validation have not been performed.
title: Exact boundary binding law for repulsive one-dimensional bosons
